minutes.headline: Parks Commission backed 28 hours for the recreation coordinator and approved a Trails grant application; skate park deal held.
minutes.summary: The Parks Commission discussed budget priorities (mainly raising the part-time recreation coordinator's hours), recreation programming, lifeguard hiring, carry-in/carry-out trash policy, grants, the skate park agreement, a possible land gift on Whalom Road, Lake Shirley parcels and the Marshall Park renovation cost estimate. Two motions were made: a temporary youth baseball banner and approval of the Trails grant submission. The skate park agreement was not approved pending concrete certification and a state determination.

public_comment.topic: Chair invited public comment at the start; the person asked declined and said they were there to listen.
Dave updated the board on the Historical Commission's grant-funded inventory of historic sites, including Marshall Park and its cave, and possible stone-structure grants and a site visit.

votes.motion: Allow the youth baseball league to put up a temporary banner at the Marshall Park entrance announcing registration, subject to checking sign bylaw compliance.
Approve submission of the Trails grant application and name Chris Ruth as land manager on the public landowner permission form.

budget_items.topic: Purchase of services and programming lines
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager raised purchase of services and allocated money for programming after the commission's priorities were passed along.
The commission wanted to raise the coordinator's hours from the current level, and settled on 28 hours while tracking hours to support future requests.
Discussed using the parks revolving fund to supplement salaries and seasonal hires; the lifeguard line goes over each year and the remainder is taken from the revolving fund.
Possible smaller grant to replace a playground surface with a town match and a state-approved vendor quote.
The schematic-design estimate came in much higher due to earthwork, boardwalk, stormwater, utilities and contingency; grants already held offset part of it.
Concern that starting pay may trail neighbouring towns or minimum wage and should be verified.

decisions.decision: Commission agreed to recommend 28 hours for the recreation coordinator as its budget priority, to be brought to the town manager.
Chair to bring revolving fund, seasonal hiring and budget topics to the town manager.
Skate park agreement not approved tonight; seek concrete certification language via town counsel, and possibly call a special meeting when the state determination arrives.
Commission conditionally interested in the Whalom Road parcel; chair to explore approaching the ZBA/developer.
Chair to contact the ad hoc committee chair to arrange a Lake Shirley site visit.
Next meeting set for the third Wednesday, February 21.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission agreed to recommend 28 hours for the part-time recreation coordinator as its budget priority, to be taken to the town manager.
The commission voted to approve submitting the Trails grant application and to name Chris Ruth as land manager on the landowner permission form.
The skate park agreement was not approved; the commission will seek concrete certification language through town counsel and may call a special meeting once the state determination arrives.
The commission expressed conditional interest in a Whalom Road parcel, and the chair will explore approaching the ZBA or developer.
A motion on a temporary youth baseball banner at Marshall Park was made, but the outcome is not audible in the recording.

why_it_matters: The coordinator's hours and the lifeguard line, which the minutes say goes over each year and is covered from the parks revolving fund, feed the Parks and Recreation budget a resident may be asked to vote on.
The Marshall Park renovation estimate, heard as much higher at schematic design, and the pending land and skate park decisions could each become a future town spending or grant-match request.
watch_next: Next Parks Commission meeting, set for the third Wednesday, February 21.
The state determination on the skate park, which may prompt a special meeting, and the town counsel's concrete certification language.
